programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: Sorry, I Didn't Know
programme.desc: Chizzy Akudolu hosts the classic panel show with a twist as four fantastically funny guests join team leaders Richard Blackwood and Eddie Kadi to take viewers on a tour of Black British history - this time it's Jonathan Ross, Gbemi Oladipo, Sukh Ojla and Remel London joining the team leaders. Insightful, educational, bold, tongue-in-cheek and above all very funny, the teams will battle over four rounds - from guessing why unknown faces from history should be famous to uncovering a treasure trove of facts about Africa, this show educates as much as it entertains with a fabulous array of comedians from all backgrounds. It's history with a touch of colour...

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.title: Die Another Day
programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, which is home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of Typhoon fighter jets - James fulfils a lifetime ambition of training in a Typhoon flight simulator before heading airside to cook up homemade crumpets with buttered lobster, spinach and samphire for the RAF staff. James next pays a visit to two ex-RAF Lossiemouth pilots who are living the dream and running their own craft brewery just down the road from their old base - he's so inspired that he takes some of their beer and uses it to make a classic comforting one-pot beef stew and dumplings. Back at Lossiemouth, Nick shows the base's young recruits some tasty recipe suggestions that they can make in their digs, and there's a surprise in store as James has arranged for him to be put through his paces at an RAF fitness test. Finally, James takes one of the area's most abundant fish and makes mackerel and cauliflower with mango dressing.

programme.title: Grantchester
programme.desc: Crime drama. Geordie is still mourning Will's departure when Mrs C charges into the pub with reports of a gentleman breaking into the vicarage - Geordie leaps into action and heads straight inside the vicarage to confront the intruder. A tussle ensues between them before Geordie is confronted by the realisation that this man is no burglar - he's the new vicar. The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church. As the Walkers leave, Albert's son Harvey accuses the Walkers of murdering his father - as Alphy corrals the two families into the vicarage and Geordie arrives to investigate, an initially reluctant Alphy finds himself drawn into solving clues and uncovering buried secrets.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: James' culinary tour of Britain continues in Scotland with a trip to Blair Castle in the Highlands, where he's joined by top Scottish Michelin-starred chef Tom Kitchin - their journey begins with an incredible tour of the castle grounds complete with awe-inspiring views. James kicks off the cooking with his venison with beetroot and blackberries in the castle's walled garden, and Tom then dusts off his wellies and heads into the woods for a bit of wild mushroom foraging - this inspires James to whip up some wild mushrooms on toast with duck eggs and British truffles before he gets a masterclass in Highland gaming as young brothers David and Harry share the secrets to the famous caber toss. James then cooks up Arbroath smokie scotch eggs with curry mayonnaise - finally, James and Tom take to the water and fish in the River Gary for wild salmon... but James' too impatient to wait for a catch, cheats, and cooks up some lovely supermarket fish in his Blair Castle salmon with saffron sauce.

programme.desc: The 20th entry in the James Bond film series and Pierce Brosnan's final appearance as the secret agent. 007 is assigned to North Korea on a mission to assassinate a colonel when he is betrayed by a double agent at MI6 and captured - after enduring 14 months of torture, James is traded at the Korean border for Zao, a North Korean agent and associate of the colonel, in a prisoner exchange. Bond then escapes his subsequent MI6 detention and tracks Zao to Havana where he meets NSA agent Jinx and learns that she is working on the same case - James soon discovers that Zao is in league with the British diamond and technology tycoon Sir Gustav Graves... and that the two are planning to use a new satellite called Icarus to change the power balance of the world permanently.

programme.desc: Festive special set between the events of the films Shrek the Third and Shrek Forever After. It is Christmas time in Shrek's swamp, but there is just one problem - Shrek has never celebrated Christmas before in his life. A copy of the book Christmas for Village Idiots sets Shrek straight, but just as it as appears as though Shrek may be able to create the perfect first Christmas with his new family with Fiona, Shrek's friends - Donkey, Puss in Boots, Gingy and the rest of the fairy-tale gang - gatecrash his house on Christmas Eve. Shrek is trying to tell a special version of The Night Before Christmas to his family, but everyone wants to add their own story to the tale, which makes Shrek more and more angry. An accident which follows leaves Shrek unable to cope with the ruining of his perfect Christmas, and he loses his temper and storms out of his shack. Can Shrek's first Christmas still be saved?

programme.title: Fred Claus
programme.desc: Fantasy comedy. Fred Claus has lived his entire life in his brother's very large shadow - he tried to match him, but he could hardly live up to the example set by the younger Nicholas, who was just perfect. The trouble with this is that Fred isn't exactly elf material... and with Christmas fast approaching Fred could yet jeopardise the jolliest holiday of the year.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Grady Felton returns home to Midsomer after serving time for the murder of local youngster Daniel Denning, and Daniel's extended family are angry at his reappearance. Later, Grady's house is firebombed, leaving him in a coma. Daniel's former friend Fred Burns is on trial for drugs offences. When Barnaby looks into Fred's background, he finds that a large sum of money appeared in Fred's bank account after the attack on Grady. As the detectives look further into the case, they discover that Grady always claimed innocence. Could a 'friend' be acting out Grady's revenge plan?

A change of circumstance puts Bertie Pelham in the limelight and Edith must decide whether to conceal her past at all costs or confront the truth and risk losing everything - as both sisters seek their perfect match, hostilities escalate and it is up to Mary to decide if she can ever make peace with Edith or herself. Meanwhile, Spratt proves to be a man of hidden talents, Mr Molesley embarks on a career in teaching though his first lesson does not quite go to plan, and will the Crawleys come to Mrs Patmore's aid when her bed and breakfast garners some unwanted attention?

programme.title: Downton Abbey

Elsewhere, Carson struggles to come to terms with new developments, Spratt's successful moonlighting venture is threatened by Denker's interference, and Daisy may have missed her chance at love.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Grady Felton returns home to Midsomer after serving time for the murder of local youngster Daniel Denning, and Daniel's extended family are angry at his reappearance. Around the time that Grady arrives, his defence barrister Giles Harrison is killed. Grady had threatened Harrison and others - including Jones - but his alibi is strong. Later, Grady's house is firebombed, leaving him in a coma. Daniel's former friend Fred Burns is on trial for drugs offences. When Barnaby looks into Fred's background, he finds that a large sum of money appeared in Fred's bank account after the attack on Grady. After the court appearance, Jones learns that another lawyer on Grady's hit-list has been killed - but since Grady is in intensive care, he could not have been the culprit. As the detectives look further into the case, they discover that Grady always claimed innocence. Could a 'friend' be acting out Grady's revenge plan?

programme.title: Jigsaw

programme.title: Fox

programme.title: An Innocent Man
programme.desc: 1989. Crime Drama. Directed by Peter Yates. Stars Tom Selleck, F. Murray Abraham & Laila Robins. Two corrupt cops send an innocent man to prison, leading him to seek revenge on his release. [S]

The man introduces himself as the Reverend Alphy Kottaram - as Alphy settles into life in Grantchester, his first order of business at the church is a funeral service for local landowner Albert Baron, who apparently took his own life - when the service is abruptly interrupted by the Walkers, a family warring with the Barons, a fight breaks out in the church.
